## Incident Report: 2024-08-15 Traffic Analysis Exercise

### Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.8.15.133 | Consistent source of all traffic below |
| MAC | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 | ARP: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.8.15.133` maps to this MAC |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV | NBNS name registration from 10.8.15.133 (`<00>`/`<20>` records); confirmed by DNS queries for `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV` / `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV.local`; Kerberos `CNameString` = `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$` |
| AD domain / workgroup | LAFONTAINEBLEU (lafontainebleu.org), DC at 10.8.15.4 (WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org) | NBNS `LAFONTAINEBLEU<00>`; CLDAP/LDAP/Kerberos SRV lookups against the DC |
| Logged-in user | plucero | Kerberos `CNameString` = `plucero` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic between 10.8.15.133 and the DC (10.8.15.4) |

### Malware Family

**DarkGate loader/RAT — behavioral attribution (not signature-confirmed).** No IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory (only the pcap was provided), so this is based purely on observed protocol behavior:

- Fake-invoice phishing delivery over HTTPS/Cloudflare-fronted infrastructure, dropping a ZIP containing an oversized (6.99 MB) obfuscated `.js` "invoice."
- The infected host then used a Microsoft BITS job (`Microsoft BITS/7.8` User-Agent) to pull a second-stage PE32+ DLL from a bare-IP host over plain HTTP, disguised with a mismatched `Content-Type: text/html`.
- The DLL then beacons continuously (308 requests over ~30 minutes) to the same bare IP on port 80, using an anomalous, malformed User-Agent (`Mozilla / 5.0 ...`, note the stray space before the slash), smuggling encrypted/encoded data in the `Cookie` header on GET requests and in binary POST bodies, with the server periodically returning `400 Bad Request`. This BITS-delivered-DLL + Cookie-encoded HTTP beacon + malformed legacy-IE UA combination is a well-documented DarkGate behavioral signature.

### Delivery Chain

1. **t=74.7s** — `10.8.15.133` (real Edge 127 browser UA) issued `GET /managements?...` to **quote.checkfedexexp.com** (resolved to 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159, Cloudflare), which returned `200 application/octet-stream`: a ZIP archive.
2. The ZIP contained **Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js**, an oversized obfuscated JScript downloader.
3. **t=135.9s** — a Windows BITS job (`Microsoft BITS/7.8` UA) issued HEAD then GET to `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`, downloading a 159,232-byte PE32+ DLL.
4. **t=196.9s onward** — the host began sustained HTTP beaconing to `72.5.43.29:80` (GET/POST `/`, no Host resolution — hardcoded IP), continuing to the end of the capture (t≈1962s).

### Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — beaconed to 308 times over ~30 minutes with GET/POST `/`, `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` UA, base64 blob in `Cookie` header, encrypted binary POST bodies, intermittent `400 Bad Request` responses (tcp streams 134, 142-…).
- Same IP also served the second-stage DLL over `/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`.

**Malicious domain**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (resolved 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159) — served the malicious ZIP. (`business.checkfedexexp.com` also resolved by the host to the same IPs at t=100s but no content transfer was observed to it in this capture — listed here for context, not confirmed as an active delivery path.)

**Malicious URL**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — ZIP download, `200 application/octet-stream`.
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — DLL payload download.

**Transferred files / hashes (SHA256, computed from objects exported out of the pcap)**
| File | SHA256 | Source |
|---|---|---|
| managements (ZIP, downloaded as octet-stream) | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` | quote.checkfedexexp.com |
| Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | extracted from the ZIP |
| 0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4 (PE32+ DLL) | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` | 72.5.43.29/data/... via BITS |

### Benign Context (not IOCs)
Microsoft/Windows OS telemetry and update infrastructure (msftconnecttest.com, MS delivery/CDN IPs 23.220.x.x/23.53.x.x/199.232.210.172/204.79.197.x, smartscreen, OCSP at oneocsp.microsoft.com, azureedge, msn/bing); Adobe ARM update check (acroipm2.adobe.com); AD/domain traffic to DC 10.8.15.4 (Kerberos, LDAP, CLDAP, DRSUAPI, SAMR, NBNS); DHCP, mDNS, LLMNR, SSDP M-SEARCH multicast noise; ARP.

### Summary
Windows workstation DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133, MAC 00:1c:bf:03:54:82), logged in as domain user "plucero" in the LAFONTAINEBLEU AD domain, was infected via a fake-FedEx-invoice phishing page (quote.checkfedexexp.com) that delivered a ZIP-wrapped obfuscated JScript downloader. The script used a BITS job to fetch a DLL from a hardcoded IP (72.5.43.29), which then established a persistent HTTP C2 beacon on port 80 to the same IP for the rest of the capture. The beacon's use of a malformed legacy-IE user agent and Cookie-header-encoded encrypted traffic is consistent with DarkGate, though this is a behavioral, not signature-confirmed, attribution since no IDS alerts accompanied this capture.
